t: This is Kensington Square, a garden square in W8. It was built from 1692 on land acquired in 1685, and it is the oldest square of its kind in Kensington. The houses facing it, numbers 1 to 45, are listed Grade II for their architecture and history. Several people have lived or died here. Patrick Wilson, a Scottish astronomer who held the chair of practical astronomy at Glasgow, died here in 1811. The cleric Robert Hamilton died here too, in 1832. Ethne Rudd and Laura Ponsonby also lived on the square.
